## Plan — Total sent under the invoices table **What changes.** Today `/invoices` lists all five invoices and shows the export button with a count, but the money is never added up. After this change one line sits directly under the table reading `Total sent: $1,497.50`, summed over exactly the invoices `exportableInvoices()` returns — the same set the button counts and the CSV contains — so the three can never disagree. The table, the button and `GET /invoices/export` are untouched. **How.** - `lib/invoices.ts` gains two pure functions: `totalCents(invoices)`, which sums `amountCents` over whatever list it is given (the page passes the already-filtered `exportable`, so the sent/paid rule stays in its one existing place), and `formatCurrency(amountCents)`, which renders a figure read on its own as `$1,497.50` via a module-level `Intl.NumberFormat("en-US", { style: "currency", currency: "USD" })` — no new dependency. - `formatAmount` is deliberately *not* widened. Every table cell calls it and must keep printing a bare `245.00`; changing it would change output nobody asked to change. If the repo later wants one money formatter with a currency option instead of two functions, that is a separate work item. - `app/invoices/page.tsx` computes `totalCents(exportable)` beside the existing `exportable` and renders one `

` after ``, with the text as a single template literal. That last detail is load-bearing: React's server renderer puts a `` marker between adjacent text children, so split JSX would serve `Total sent: $1,497.50`. **Files the build may touch:** `lib/invoices.ts`, `app/invoices/page.tsx`, `lib/invoices.test.ts`, `app/invoices/page.test.tsx` (new). **Acceptance checks.** 1. Open ` (localhost/redacted) directly below the table is a line reading exactly `Total sent: $1,497.50\` — dollar sign, thousands comma, two decimals. 2. \`curl -s (localhost/redacted) contains that literal string unbroken in the HTML. 3. The total counts the same set as the button: the button reads `Export 3 invoices as CSV`, the table still lists INV-1004 (draft) and INV-1005 (void), and the total reads $1,497.50 — not $2,878.50, which is what counting the draft and the void would give. 4. ` curl -s -D- (localhost/redacted) is unchanged: 200, `text/csv; charset=utf-8\`, header row plus exactly three data rows, no INV-1004 or INV-1005. **Tests.** New `totalCents` and `formatCurrency` blocks in `lib/invoices.test.ts` (the only existing test file this touches), using the existing `invoice(over)` factory; a new `app/invoices/page.test.tsx` renders the page in jsdom and asserts the total line is there and that `$2,878.50` is not. The page test also keeps the changed lines in `app/` above the 80% diff-coverage floor — nothing renders that page today. **Checked beforehand:** `Intl.NumberFormat("en-US", ...)` returns exactly `$1,497.50` on this runner; `24500 + 118000 + 7250 = 149750`, matching the figure in the request; a throwaway probe confirmed `(InvoicesPage /)` renders under the repo's existing vitest/jsdom setup; and the React server-render marker behaviour above was reproduced with `renderToString`. This is visible, not gated — no approval step. If the figure or the wording is wrong, say so on this issue. > Generated by [Spec](https://github.com/bsf-fixtures/ts-webapp/actions/runs/44844580848) · claude · opus50 · \~79 AIC · ⌖ \~22 AIC · ⊞ 2.6K · [◷](https://github.com/search?q=repo%3Absf-fixtures%2Fts-webapp+%22gh-aw-workflow-call-id%3A+bsf-fixtures%2Fts-webapp%2Ffactory-role-spec%22&type=issues)
